summary: RE-TEST of the reconcile_followups() race-condition fix (asyncio.Lock serialization + partial unique index on followups.source_key) reported in iteration_12. Independently re-verified via: (1) re-run of the previously-failing regression test test_no_duplicate_source_keys_for_tiles_rules — now PASSES; (2) full 11-test test_followups_v2_workspaces.py suite — all 11 pass (2 later became data-dependent SKIPs once the last open selection_waiting card was consumed by the auto-close test, expected, not a bug); (3) a new independent stress test (test_reconcile_race_condition.py) firing 5 genuinely concurrent POST /api/followups/reconcile via httpx+asyncio.gather — zero duplicate (rule_type, quotation_id) rows resulted; (4) direct MongoDB verification script confirming the partial unique index `followups_source_key_unique` (partialFilterExpression source_key is string) actually exists on the live followups collection AND an aggregation over the whole collection (any status) found ZERO duplicate source_key groups (178 total followups, 129 automated); (5) re-ran the exact approve->move-to-quotation->reconcile sequence — exactly one quotation_tiles_waiting card resulted and the prior selection_waiting card correctly flipped to status=done/auto_resolved=true. CONFIRMED: the CRITICAL race condition is fixed at both the application-lock layer and the database-constraint layer. One secondary finding: under 5 truly concurrent reconcile calls, 2/5 returned HTTP 502 (Cloudflare gateway) because reconcile takes ~20s per full pass and the new lock serializes them (queued calls can exceed the gateway's timeout) — this does NOT cause data corruption (zero duplicates either way) but is a latency/availability side-effect worth the main agent's awareness. Also re-confirmed the pre-existing LOW-priority place-order/confirm test failure is UNCHANGED (same KeyError: 'purchase_orders', out of scope). Automation-rules config GET still returns exactly 2 seeded rows (selection [2,4,7,10], quotation_tiles [2,5,10,15]); WhatsApp templates still byte-exact; workspace_counts still present with correct keys/types.

minor.issue: The race-condition fix (process-local asyncio.Lock + partial unique index) correctly eliminates duplicate cards, but as a side-effect, concurrent/overlapping reconcile calls now fully serialize behind the lock instead of running in parallel. Since a single full reconcile pass takes ~19-20s against current data volume (scans all quotations + purchase_orders + shortages + customers), firing 5 concurrent calls caused 2/5 to receive HTTP 502 (Cloudflare gateway timeout) while waiting in the lock queue. No data corruption resulted (verified zero duplicates), but this is a latency/availability trade-off of the fix worth noting — e.g. if the frontend's bootstrap() fires reconcile on every Follow-ups page load while multiple staff have the page open, some of those requests could now 502 under load instead of just being slow.

Response shape no longer includes a top-level purchase_orders key. Pre-existing, unrelated to Follow-ups 2.0/race-condition scope — not touched this session per instructions, just re-confirmed status quo.

critical_code_review_comments: services/followup_engine.py: the asyncio.Lock() fix is correct and minimal — wraps the entire read-desired/read-existing/write loop in a single critical section, so overlapping calls now see each other's writes. Comment block above it (lines 319-331) accurately documents the original bug and the fix rationale.

scripts/ensure_indexes.py: the new followups_source_key_unique partial unique index (partialFilterExpression source_key is string) is correctly scoped to exclude manual follow-ups (source_key=null) via sparse-style filtering, and _safe_create_index's existing DUPLICATE_KEY_CODE handling means it would have logged rather than crashed had any duplicate survived — verified live that it applied cleanly with zero violations.

The lock is process-local (in-memory asyncio.Lock) — correct for the current single-backend-instance deployment, but would NOT serialize calls across multiple backend processes/pods if this app is ever horizontally scaled. The DB unique index is the real backstop in that scenario (an insert would fail with a duplicate key error instead of silently creating a dupe) — but the current code around the insert (services/followup_engine.py 594-595) does not appear to catch/handle a DuplicateKeyError, so a future multi-instance deployment could see a raw 500 on the losing writer instead of a graceful no-op. Not an issue today (single instance), but worth flagging for future scaling.
